solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: School principal wants to expel German music fan

parts.note: the head is the person in charge of a school
to ban someone is to exclude or expel them

explanation.surface: A head teacher is keen to throw a German pupil out of school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants to' is just link words: the head wants to ban the German.
explanation.definitionFit: A headbanger is a heavy-metal devotee who shakes their head violently in time to the music.

clue.text: Steamier parts in Middle Eastern region

indicators.note: the word steamier is split into parts and its letters reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Some places in the Middle East are steamier than others.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Arab Emirates is a federation of states on the Gulf, a region of the Middle East.

clue.text: Turkey salad you served finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the three words salad, you and served

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the salad you eventually brought was a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letters of salad, you and served.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is slang for a failure or flop, as is a dud.

clue.text: In rear part of boat, look up

indicators.note: In tells us the word for look goes inside the word for the back of a boat

parts.note: aft is the stern end of a ship
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone at the stern of a boat is told to look upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means high overhead, in the air or up in a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Plant is potted by man before start of autumn

indicators.note: potted by means put inside, as a plant is held within a pot, so is goes into the word for man

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman or man

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of the word autumn

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a shrub in a pot just before autumn arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potted' suits the gardening picture but here signals one piece held inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Genista is the broom genus, a yellow-flowered shrub, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: They love traveller's tricks?

parts.note: a Rom is a Romany man, a traveller; the possessive is read as 'traveller has'
antics are pranks or tricks

explanation.surface: The question is whether a gypsy's pranks make him lovable.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: romantics are people given to love.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantics are idealistic people devoted to love and passion, so they are the ones who love.

clue.text: Polish females attending British university

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the letters for females sit beside the others

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Polish women are studying at a British university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality, but it is the verb meaning to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: To buff a surface is to rub it until it shines, which is to polish it.

clue.text: Rich person's bitterness about cat show

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for bitterness wraps the other pieces

parts.note: bile is bitterness or bad temper
a lion is a big cat
to air an opinion is to show it publicly

explanation.surface: A wealthy person resents a cat show.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionaire has wealth of at least a thousand million, an extremely wealthy individual.

clue.text: Hunt over a long period

parts.note: for and over both introduce a span of time, as in for a week or over a week
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A search goes on and on for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search about for food or supplies, which is to hunt for them.

clue.text: Chill breeze no longer blowing?

definitions.meaning: to chill is to relax and unwind
a breeze that has dropped away, read literally as the wind having gone down

explanation.surface: A cold breeze has stopped blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Winding down means relaxing, and the phrase read literally describes the wind easing off.

clue.text: Gentleman abroad abandoned limo by side of road

indicators.note: by side of means placed next to, so the abbreviation for road follows the rearranged limo
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters of limo run loose

explanation.surface: A gentleman leaves his limousine beside the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges LIMO to MILO, set 'by side of' RD, short for road.
explanation.definitionFit: Milord is how continental Europeans traditionally addressed an English nobleman travelling abroad.

clue.text: Empty container inside larger one?

indicators.note: inside means the smaller container sits within the bigger one

parts.note: a vat is a big container, larger than a can
a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: An empty tin is nested inside a bigger container.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied or empty, as of a room or seat.

clue.text: Predicting a non-academic grade?

parts.note: dumb means unintelligent, humorously the opposite of academic
a rating is a grade or score

explanation.surface: A school report forecasts a poor non-academic grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to foreshadow or indicate faintly in advance, close to predicting.

clue.text: Son and I twice spotted in US coastal location

parts.note: I is given a second time as ego, the Latin for I

explanation.surface: A parent and son were twice seen at some American seaside spot.
explanation.walkthrough: I appears twice: once as itself and again as EGO, Latin for 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a Californian city on the Pacific coast near the Mexican border.

clue.text: Travelling to UN, Remainer finds reward

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of to UN and Remainer shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A pro-EU voter heads to the United Nations and is paid for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' rearranges TO UN REMAINER. A Remainer voted for Britain to stay in the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Remuneration is payment for work or services, a form of reward.

clue.text: Prophet briefly enlisting support for woman

indicators.note: enlisting means taking on board, so the shortened name holds the word for support
briefly means cut short, so the prophet's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Elisha was an Old Testament prophet, successor to Elijah
to abet is to support or assist

explanation.surface: A prophet, in short, recruits help for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the prophet's final letter before the support goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisabeth is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Presentation of certain films, American works

indicators.note: works means is worked into a new form, so the letters of American are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some films are screened at an American factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinerama was a widescreen process projecting films from three projectors onto a curved screen.

clue.text: Line one actor (Irish) gets in small part in play

indicators.note: gets in means is admitted to, so the group of pieces goes inside the word for a small part

parts.note: a bit part is a small acting role
I is the Roman numeral for one
a thesp, short for thespian, is an actor

explanation.surface: An Irish actor lands a single line in a minor role in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe Spirit is a comedy by Noël Coward about a ghostly first wife.

clue.text: Great uncertainty discussed in secret location

indicators.note: discussed means spoken about, so the words for great uncertainty are heard rather than seen

parts.note: great is high and uncertainty is doubt, giving high doubt

explanation.surface: Deep doubts are talked over at a secret meeting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discussed' says HIGH DOUBT out loud, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a hiding place, somewhere secret to escape notice.

clue.text: Complain about rise of Internet leading to trouble

indicators.note: leading to means coming first, so the reversed piece stands before the next
in a down entry a rise reads upwards, so the word for Internet runs backwards

parts.note: the web is the Internet
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone moans that the growth of the Internet causes problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' reverses WEB to give BEW; 'leading to' puts it ahead of AIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewail is to lament or express great sorrow over something, a strong way to complain.

clue.text: Phone a female about assistance with case

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the joined pieces run in the opposite direction

parts.note: to dial is to phone
gel is a posh pronunciation of girl, a female

explanation.surface: Someone rings a woman for help with a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is public funding to help people pay for advice or representation in a court case.

clue.text: Take new view, perhaps, backing Guardian

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for a fresh look runs backwards

parts.note: to re-peek would be to take another look, a fresh view

explanation.surface: A guardian reconsiders and supports a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses RE-PEEK, an invented word for 'look again'; 'perhaps' warns of this.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper is someone who guards or looks after something, such as a zookeeper or goalkeeper.

clue.text: Executioner's craft

definitions.meaning: Jack ... was a notorious 17th-century English hangman, whose name became slang for any executioner
a boat: a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: The skill of a hangman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a skill, but it is a boat; the 's joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ketch was a famous hangman, and a ketch is also a two-masted sailing boat.

clue.text: Mischievous girl at home in rugby or cricket, say.

indicators.note: in places the word for at home inside the word for a sport

parts.note: rugby and cricket are examples of a game
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A cheeky girl plays rugby or cricket at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamine is a slim, elfin girl with an impish, boyish charm.

clue.text: End of treatment after surgery here in France by an eye specialist

indicators.note: after means following, so the letter from treatment comes behind the word for surgery

parts.note: op is short for operation, surgery

indicators.note: End of takes the final letter of the word treatment

parts.note: ici is French for here

explanation.surface: After surgery in France, treatment ends with a visit to an eye doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician tests eyesight and prescribes glasses, a specialist in eyes.

clue.text: My business partner's last letter

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: last letter picks out the closing letter of partner, ignoring the possessive

explanation.surface: A trader receives the final letter from a business partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive here but an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!' or 'gosh!'.

clue.text: Record with loud beat

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A record with a loud drumbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to whip or thrash, which is to beat.

clue.text: Thora and Edith prepared to leave

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the two names are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Two women get ready to set off.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the road is an idiom for setting off on a journey, departing.
